Tranilast is given to children for the prophylactic management of asthma, in allergic rhinitis and eczema, and in the management of keloids and hypertrophic scars. An oral daily dose of 5 mg/kg, given in 3 divided doses, may be used. Sarcoidosis. For a mention of possible benefit from tranilast in cutaneous sarcoidosis, see p.1512. Profile Tretoquinol is a direct-acting sympathomimetic reported to have a selective action on beta2 receptors (a beta2 agonist). It has prop- erties similar to those of salbutamol (p.1131). It is given as the hydrochloride for its bronchodilating properties in the manage- ment of reversible airways obstruction, as in asthma (p.1108) or in some patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (p.1112).
